Event ID: 114 (Derived from Section 4.4.2.1)
Sentence: "Before security can be activated, the AMF and the UE need to establish a 5G NAS security context. Usually, the 5G NAS security context is created as the result of a primary authentication and key agreement procedure between the AMF and the UE. A new 5G NAS security context may also be created during an N1 mode to N1 mode handover. Alternatively, during inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode, the AMF not supporting interworking without N26 and the UE operating in single-registration mode may derive a mapped 5G NAS security context from an EPS security context that has been established while the UE was in S1 mode"
Start State: No 5G NAS security context exists between the AMF and the UE.
Condition: Security activation is required, or a handover/inter-system change occurs.

End State: A 5G NAS security context is established between the AMF and the UE, enabling secure communication.

Event ID: 115 (Derived from Section 4.4.2.1)
Sentence: "The 5G NAS security context is taken into use by the UE and the AMF, when the AMF initiates a security mode control procedure, during an N1 mode to N1 mode handover, or during the inter-system change procedure from S1 mode to N1 mode. The 5G NAS security context which has been taken into use by the network most recently is called current 5G NAS security context. This current 5G NAS security context can be of type native or mapped, i.e. originating from a native 5G NAS security context or mapped 5G NAS security context"
Start State: The UE and AMF have an existing 5G NAS security context, but it is not yet in use.
Condition: The AMF initiates a security mode control procedure, an N1 mode to N1 mode handover, or an inter-system change procedure from S1 mode to N1 mode.
Action: The 5G NAS security context is activated and taken into use by both the UE and the AMF. The most recently used 5G NAS security context is designated as the current 5G NAS security context, which can be either native or mapped.
End State: The current 5G NAS security context is in use, and it is classified as either native or mapped based on its origin.
============================================================
Event ID: 116 (Derived from Section 4.4.2.1)
Sentence: "The key set identifier ngKSI is assigned by the AMF either during the primary authentication and key agreement procedure or, for the mapped 5G NAS security context, during the inter-system change. The ngKSI consists of a value and a type of security context parameter indicating whether a 5G NAS security context is a native 5G NAS security context or a mapped 5G NAS security context. When the 5G NAS security context is a native 5G NAS security context, the ngKSI has the value of KSIAMF, and when the current 5G NAS security context is of type mapped, the ngKSI has the value of KSIASME"
Start State: The 5G NAS security context is either not established or requires an update (e.g., during primary authentication or inter-system change).
Condition: The AMF initiates the primary authentication and key agreement procedure or an inter-system change occurs, requiring the assignment of ngKSI.
Action: The AMF assigns the ngKSI, which includes a value (KSIAMF for native or KSIASME for mapped) and a type parameter indicating the security context type (native or mapped).
End State: The ngKSI is successfully assigned, and the 5G NAS security context is updated with the appropriate value and type.

Event ID: 1413 (Derived from Section 4.16)
Sentence: "UE radio capability signalling optimisation (RACS) is a feature that is optional at both the UE and the network and which aims to optimise the transmission of UE radio capability over the radio interface (see 3GPPTS23.501[8]). RACS works by assigning an identifier to represent a set of UE radio capabilities. This identifier is called the UE radio capability ID. A UE radio capability ID can be either manufacturer-assigned or network-assigned. The UE radio capability ID is an alternative to the signalling of the radio capabilities container over the radio interface"
Start State: UE radio capabilities are typically transmitted in their entirety over the radio interface, which may lead to inefficiencies in signalling.
Condition: The UE and network support the optional RACS feature, and there is a need to optimise the transmission of UE radio capabilities.
Action: The RACS feature assigns a UE radio capability ID (either manufacturer-assigned or network-assigned) to represent a set of UE radio capabilities, replacing the need to transmit the full radio capabilities container over the radio interface.
End State: The UE radio capability ID is used as an optimised alternative to transmitting the full radio capabilities container, reducing signalling overhead over the radio interface.

Event ID: 1553 (Derived from Section 4.24)
Sentence: "b) if the UE has a stored disaster roaming wait range, the UE shall generate a random number within the disaster roaming wait range and start a timer with the generated random number. While the timer is running, the UE shall not initiate registration on the selected PLMN except if the UE needs to request an emergency PDU session, in which case the UE shall initiate the registration procedure, set the 5GS registration type IE to "emergency registration" in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message and keep the timer running. Start State: UE has a stored disaster roaming wait range and is camped on a selected PLMN.
Condition: UE has a stored disaster roaming wait range.
Action: When the UE has a stored disaster roaming wait range, it shall generate a random number within that range and start a timer using the generated value. While the timer is active, the UE shall not initiate a registration procedure on the selected PLMN, except when it needs to request an emergency PDU session. In that case, the UE shall initiate the registration procedure, set the 5GS registration type IE to “emergency registration” in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message, and keep the timer running. When the timer expires, if the UE does not have an emergency PDU session, it shall perform the registration procedure for disaster roaming services as described in clause 5.5.1, provided it is still camped on the selected PLMN. If the UE has an emergency PDU session when the timer expires, it shall perform the registration procedure for disaster roaming services after releasing the emergency PDU session, assuming it is still camped on the selected PLMN.
End State: The UE either performs the registration procedure for disaster roaming services immediately after the timer expires or defers the procedure until the emergency PDU session is released, ensuring proper synchronization with the selected PLMN.

Event ID: 2178 (Derived from Section 5.3.3)
Sentence: "A temporary user identity for 5GS-based services, the 5G globally unique temporary identity (5G-GUTI), is used for identification within the signalling procedures. In case of PLMN the 5G-GUTI is globally unique and in case of SNPN the 5G-GUTI is unique within an SNPN. When the UE is registered to the same PLMN or SNPN over 3GPP and non-3GPP access, the UE and the AMF maintain one 5G-GUTI that is common to both 3GPP and non-3GPP access. When the UE is required to delete the 5G-GUTI according to a NAS procedure, the UE shall delete the 5G-GUTI only if it is not registered to the same PLMN or SNPN through other access. When the UE is registered to different PLMNs or SNPNs over 3GPP access and non-3GPP access, the UE maintains two 5G-GUTIs, a 5G-GUTI for the registration with a PLMN or SNPN over the 3GPP access and another 5G-GUTI for the registration with another PLMN or SNPN over the non-3GPP access. In the paging and service request procedures, a shortened form of the 5G-GUTI, the 5G S-temporary mobile subscriber identity (5G-S-TMSI), is used to enable more efficient radio signalling. The purpose of the 5G-GUTI and 5G-S-TMSI is to provide identity confidentiality, i.e., to protect a user from being identified and located by an intruder. The structure of the 5G-GUTI and its derivatives are specified in 3GPPTS23.003[4]. The 5G-GUTI has two main components (see 3GPPTS23.501[8])"
Start State: The UE is registered to a PLMN or SNPN, and the 5G-GUTI is assigned for identification within signalling procedures.
Condition: The UE is required to delete the 5G-GUTI according to a NAS procedure.
Action: The UE deletes the 5G-GUTI only if it is not registered to the same PLMN or SNPN through
End State: Not specified

Event ID: 2325 (Derived from Section 5.3.6)
Sentence: "If the UE requested the use of active time by including an active time value and the network accepts the use of MICO mode and the use of active time, the AMF shall include an active time value in the T3324 IE to the UE. If the AMF indicates active time value to the UE, AMF should not indicate "all PLMN registration area allocated" indication in the MICO indication IE to the UE. Upon entering 5GMM-IDLE mode, AMF shall start the active timer with the active time value indicated to the UE and shall consider the UE is reachable for paging as long as the timer is running. If the UE enters 5GMM-CONNECTED mode over 3GPP access when the active timer is running, the AMF shall stop the active timer"
Start State: UE has requested the use of active time by including an active time value, and the network has accepted the use of MICO mode and active time.
Condition: The UE enters 5GMM-IDLE mode or 5GMM-CONNECTED mode over 3GPP access.
Action: If the UE requested active time and the network approved it, the AMF shall include the active time value in the T3324 IE provided to the UE. When the AMF indicates the active time value to the UE, it shall not set the “all PLMN registration area allocated” indication in the MICO indication IE. When the UE enters 5GMM-IDLE mode, the AMF shall start the active timer using the active time value and shall treat the UE as reachable for paging as long as the timer is running. If the UE subsequently enters 5GMM-CONNECTED mode over 3GPP access while the active timer is active, the AMF shall stop the active timer immediately.
End State: The AMF manages the active timer based on the UE’s mode: In 5GMM-IDLE mode, the active timer runs, and the UE remains reachable for paging. Upon entering 5GMM-CONNECTED mode, the active timer stops, and the UE is no longer paged using the active-time mechanism.

Sentence: "The control plane CIoT 5GS optimization enables support of efficient transport of user data (IP, Ethernet and Unstructured) or SMS messages over control plane via the AMF without triggering user-plane resources establishment. Optional header compression of IP data and Ethernet data can be applied to PDU sessions with IP PDU session type and Ethernet PDU session type that are configured to support header compression. The network selects the back-off timer value to avoid synchronized timeouts among UEs.
End State: The REGISTRATION ACCEPT message is sent to the UE, including the Extended rejected NSSAI IE with the rejection cause and optionally a back-off timer for each S-NSSAI. The UE is informed of the rejection and may defer further requests based on the back-off timer.

Action: The network includes the rejected S-NSSAI(s) in the Extended rejected NSSAI IE of the REGISTRATION REJECT message if the ER-NSSAI bit is set; otherwise, it includes the rejected S-NSSAI(s) in the Rejected NSSAI IE of the REGISTRATION REJECT message.
End State: The REGISTRATION REJECT message is sent to the UE with the rejected S-NSSAI(s) included in the appropriate IE (Extended rejected NSSAI IE or Rejected NSSAI IE).

Event ID: 6199 (Derived from Section 5.5.2.3.2)
Sentence: "Upon receiving the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message, if the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message indicates "re-registration required" and the de-registration request is for 3GPP access, the UE shall perform a local release of the PDU sessions over 3GPP access, if any. If a PDU session is associated with one or more MBS sessions, the UE shall locally leave the associated MBS sessions. If there is an MA PDU session with user plane resources established on both 3GPP access and non-3GPP access in the same PLMN or in different PLMNs, the UE shall perform a local release of the user plane resources on 3GPP access. If the MA PDU session is associated with one or more MBS sessions, the UE shall locally leave the associated MBS sessions. The UE shall stop the timer(s) T3346, T3396, T3584, T3585 and 5GSM back-off timer(s) not related to congestion control (see subclause6.2.12), if running. If the UE is operating in single-registration mode, the UE shall also stop the ESM back-off timer(s) not related to congestion control (see subclause6.3.6 in 3GPPTS24.301[15]), if running. The UE shall send a DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message to the network and enter the state 5GMM-DEREGISTERED for 3GPP access. Furthermore, the UE shall, after the completion of the de-registration procedure, and the release of the existing NAS signalling connection, if any Tsor-cm timer(s) were running and have stopped, the UE shall attempt to obtain service on a higher priority PLMN (see 3GPPTS23.122[5]) on 3GPP access, otherwise initiate an initial registration. The UE should also re-establish any previously established PDU sessions over 3GPP access. For any previously established MA PDU sessions with user plane resources established on both accesses the UE should also re-establish the user plane resources over 3GPP access, and for any previously established MA PDU sessions with user plane resources established only on the 3GPP access the UE should re-establish the MA PDU session over 3GPP access"

Action: If the UE is not operating in SNPN access operation mode, it shall store the current TAI in the list of “5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming”. Otherwise, if the UE is operating in SNPN access operation mode, it shall store the current TAI in the list of “5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming” for the current SNPN and, if the UE supports access to an SNPN using credentials from a credentials holder, it shall also store the current TAI in the selected entry of the “list of subscriber data” or the selected PLMN subscription.
End State: The current TAI is stored in the appropriate list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming" based on the UE's operation mode and configuration.

Action: The UE sends a PDU Session Establishment Request message to the AMF, which includes parameters such as DNN, SSC mode, and PDU session type. The AMF processes the request, interacts with the SMF, and establishes the PDU session.
End State: A PDU session is successfully established, and the UE can transmit and receive data over the established session.

Event ID: 7439 (Derived from Section 6.2.3)
Sentence: "c) the UE-requested PDU session modification procedure"
Start State: The UE has an established PDU session with the network.
Condition: The UE initiates a request to modify the parameters of the existing PDU session.
Action: The UE sends a PDU Session Modification Request message to the AMF, which forwards it to the SMF. The SMF processes the request, updates the session parameters, and responds with a PDU Session Modification Command. The UE acknowledges the modification with a PDU Session Modification Complete message.
End State: The PDU session parameters are updated according to the UE's request, and the session remains active with the new configuration.

Event ID: 7440 (Derived from Section 6.2.3)

Condition: The network identifies a need to modify the PDU session (e.g., due to QoS changes, traffic routing updates, or policy updates).
Action: The network initiates the PDU session modification procedure by sending a PDU Session Modification Command to the UE, which includes the required modifications. The UE processes the command and responds with a PDU Session Modification Complete message.
End State: The PDU session is updated with the new parameters, and both the UE and the network operate with the modified session configuration.

Sentence: "b) Collision of UE-requested PDU session release procedure and a PDU session authentication and authorization procedure"
Start State: UE has an active PDU session, and both the UE-requested PDU session release procedure and the PDU session authentication and authorization procedure are initiated.
Condition: Simultaneous initiation of the UE-requested PDU session release procedure and the PDU session authentication and authorization procedure.
Action: The network resolves the collision by prioritizing one procedure over the other, typically by aborting or suspending the PDU session authentication and authorization procedure to allow the UE-requested PDU session release to proceed.
End State: The PDU session is released, and the PDU session authentication and authorization procedure is either aborted or suspended.

Event ID: 8203 (Derived from Section 6.3.2.5)
Sentence: "c) Collision of UE-requested PDU session release procedure and network-requested PDU session modification procedure"
Start State: Both the UE and the network are actively involved in NAS procedures—the UE is initiating a PDU session release, while the network is initiating a PDU session modification.
Condition: The UE sends a PDU SESSION RELEASE REQUEST message, and the network sends a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message simultaneously or nearly simultaneously, causing a procedural collision.
Action: The collision is detected, and the network resolves it by prioritizing one procedure over the other, typically favoring the network-requested PDU session modification procedure. The UE aborts its PDU session release procedure and processes the network's modification command.
End State: The PDU session modification procedure is completed, and the PDU session remains active with the updated parameters. The UE-requested PDU session release procedure is terminated without completion.
============================================================
Event ID: 8204 (Derived from Section 6.3.2.5)
Sentence: "If the SMF receives a PDU SESSION RELEASE REQUEST message during the network-requested PDU session modification procedure, and the PDU session indicated in the PDU SESSION RELEASE REQUEST message is the PDU session that the SMF had requested to modify, the SMF shall abort the PDU session modification procedure and proceed with the UE-requested PDU session release procedure"
Start State: The SMF is in the process of performing a network-requested PDU session modification procedure.
Condition: The SMF receives a PDU SESSION RELEASE REQUEST message, and the PDU session indicated in the message is the same PDU session that the SMF is currently modifying.
Action: The SMF aborts the ongoing PDU session modification procedure and initiates the UE-requested PDU session release procedure.
End State: The PDU session modification procedure is terminated, and the PDU session release procedure is in progress.
============================================================
Event ID: 8205 (Derived from Section 6.3.2.5)
Sentence: "d) Collision of UE-requested PDU session modification procedure and network-requested PDU session modification procedure"
Start State: Both the UE and the network have initiated PDU session modification procedures independently.
Condition: The UE and the network simultaneously attempt to modify the same PDU session.
Action: The collision is detected, and the network resolves the conflict by prioritizing one of the modification procedures, typically the network-requested procedure, as per 3GPP TS 24.301 and TS 24.501.
End State: The prioritized PDU session modification procedure is executed, and the other procedure is either terminated or postponed.

The network shall proceed with the network-requested PDU session modification procedure as if no PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message was received from the UE"
Start State: PDU SESSION MODIFICATION PENDING
Condition: The network receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message during the network-requested PDU session modification procedure, and the PDU session indicated in the message is the same as the one the network had requested to modify.

End State: The network continues the network-requested PDU session modification procedure as if no PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message was received.

Event ID: 8713 (Derived from Section 6.4.1.3)

If the received Rejection cause is set to "MBS session has not started or will not start soon" and an MBS back-off timer value is included with value that indicates neither zero nor deactivated, the UE shall start a back-off timer T3530 with the value provided in the MBS back-off timer value for the received TMGI, and shall not attempt to join the MBS session with the same TMGI until the expiry of T3530. Condition: The MBS decision is set to "MBS join is rejected".

If the Rejection cause is “User is outside of local MBS service area”, the UE shall not request to join the same MBS session while camping on a cell outside the received MBS service area. If the Rejection cause is “MBS session has not started or will not start soon” and the MBS back-off timer value is included with a value indicating neither zero nor deactivated, the UE shall start the back-off timer T3530 with the provided value for the received TMGI and shall not attempt to join the MBS session with the same TMGI until T3530 expires. If the MBS back-off timer value indicates that the timer is deactivated, the UE shall not attempt to join the MBS session with the same TMGI until the UE is switched off, the USIM is removed, or the entry in the “list of subscriber data” for the current SNPN is updated. However, if the MBS back-off timer value indicates zero, the UE may immediately attempt to join the MBS session again with the same TMGI.

Event ID: 9286 (Derived from Section 6.4.3.5)
Sentence: "The UE shall, on the first expiry of the timer T3582, retransmit the PDU SESSION RELEASE REQUEST message and the PDU session information which was transported together with the initial transmission of the PDU SESSION RELEASE REQUEST message and shall reset and start timer T3582. This retransmission is repeated four times, i.e. on the fifth expiry of timer T3582, the UE shall abort the procedure, release the allocated PTI, perform a local release of the PDU session, and perform the registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update by sending a REGISTRATION REQUEST message including the PDU session status IE over each access that user plane resources have been established if the PDU session is an MA PDU session, or over the access the PDU session is associated with if the PDU session is a single access PDU session. If there is one or more MBS multicast sessions associated with the PDU session, the UE shall locally leave the associated MBS multicast sessions"
Start State: The UE has initiated a PDU session release procedure and is waiting for a response, with timer T3582 running.
Condition: The first expiry of timer T3582 occurs.
Action: The UE retransmits the PDU SESSION RELEASE REQUEST message along with the associated PDU session information, resets and restarts timer T3582. This retransmission process is repeated four times. On the fifth expiry of timer T3582, the UE aborts the procedure, releases the allocated PTI, performs a local release of the PDU session, and initiates the registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update by sending a REGISTRATION REQUEST message including the PDU session status IE over the relevant access(es). If the PDU session is associated with MBS multicast sessions, the UE locally leaves those sessions.
End State: The PDU session is locally released, the PTI is released, and the UE has initiated a registration procedure. If applicable, the UE has left associated MBS multicast sessions.

Event ID: 9287 (Derived from Section 6.4.3.5)
Sentence: "b) Collision of UE-requested PDU session release procedure and network-requested PDU session modification procedure"
Start State: A PDU session is active, and both the UE and the network are independently initiating procedures related to the same PDU session.
Condition: The UE initiates a PDU session release procedure while the network simultaneously initiates a PDU session modification procedure for the same PDU session.
Action: The NAS layer detects the collision between the UE-requested PDU session release and the network-requested PDU session modification. The procedures are handled according to the rules defined in 3GPP TS 24.301 and TS 24.501 to resolve the conflict.
End State: The PDU session is either released or modified based on the resolution of the collision, and the NAS state is updated accordingly.
